prompt: What are the two halves of continuous integration, as the lesson defines it?

choices.text: Writing tests first and deploying daily
choices.why: Deploying is lesson 7; test-first is a different method.

choices.text: Merge daily; check every merge
choices.why: Right. The practice and the machine that makes it cheap.

choices.text: A build server and a test framework
choices.why: Those are tools; the lesson starts from the practice.

choices.text: Code review and pair programming
choices.why: Useful, but not what the term means.

prompt: Why does the lab's post-receive hook not stop a broken commit reaching main?

choices.text: Because it does not run the tests
choices.why: It runs them in six cells.

choices.text: Because its exit status is ignored by uv
choices.why: uv only builds the environments.

choices.text: It runs after the push has been accepted
choices.why: Right. It reports after the fact; a check on the pull request reports before the merge.

choices.text: Because it only checks branches other than main
choices.why: It checks only main.

prompt: How many cells did each run of the lab's CI have?
Every line the hook printed reached Ana prefixed with ___ : .
Why did the carrier test pass on the laptop and fail in every CI cell?

choices.text: Because the CI uses a different Python
choices.why: It failed in all three Pythons alike.

choices.text: The CSV was never committed
choices.why: Right. The clean checkout had the test and not its data.

choices.text: Because the CSV had a negative price
choices.why: Both prices in it were positive.

choices.text: Because the CI ran in UTC
choices.why: The São Paulo cells failed too.

prompt: In git status --short, an untracked file is marked with ___ .
Which of these does a clean checkout catch? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A dependency installed by hand and never pinned
choices.why: Right. The fresh environment installs only what is pinned.

choices.text: A file the code reads that was never committed
choices.why: Right. That was run 2.

choices.text: An environment variable set only in a shell profile
choices.why: Right. The CI has none of the author's profile.

choices.text: A rule whose expected value in the test is wrong
choices.why: A wrong expectation fails or passes the same everywhere.

prompt: A self-hosted runner reuses its working directory between runs to save time. What can go wrong?

choices.text: Nothing, since git checkout replaces every file
choices.why: git leaves untracked files from the last run in place.

choices.text: A leftover file lets a bad run pass
choices.why: Right. It passes for the same reason the laptop did.

choices.text: The runner refuses to start
choices.why: It starts; that is the problem.

choices.text: The tests run twice
choices.why: Reuse does not duplicate runs.

prompt: What did the hook do with the push of try-new-rounding?

choices.text: Ran the six cells
choices.why: It only runs for main.

choices.text: Rejected the push
choices.why: The branch reached the remote.

choices.text: Said it had nothing to run
choices.why: Right. The trigger is a push to main.

choices.text: Merged it into main
choices.why: A hook does not merge.

prompt: Match each trigger to its typical use.

pairs.right: Check a change before it merges

prompt: Why does this repository's CI run on push to main as well as on pull requests to main?

choices.text: Because pull_request runs do not test code
choices.why: They do; the question is what they test.

choices.text: Two green changes clash once combined
choices.why: Right. The push run checks the merged result.

choices.text: To run the release on every merge
choices.why: The release runs on tags.

choices.text: Because GitHub requires both
choices.why: Nothing requires it; it is a choice.

prompt: A workflow filtered by paths: does not run on a docs-only pull request, and that check is required. What happens to the pull request?

choices.text: It merges, since nothing relevant changed
choices.why: The required check never reports, so the merge stays blocked.

choices.text: The check reports skipped and passes
choices.why: Skipped is what an if on a job reports; a filtered workflow reports nothing.

choices.text: It waits for a result that never arrives
choices.why: Right. That is why this repository decides inside the workflow, with if on each job.

choices.text: GitHub runs the workflow anyway after an hour
choices.why: No such fallback exists.

prompt: How does a CI service decide that a step failed?

choices.text: By its exit status
choices.why: Right. Zero is success; anything else is failure.

choices.text: By searching its output for the word error
choices.why: The output is not read.

choices.text: By counting red lines in the log
choices.why: Colour means nothing to the service.

choices.text: By comparing its duration with the last run
choices.why: Duration does not decide success.

prompt: With set -o pipefail, what exit status did pytest -m smoke | tee run.log report?
A GitHub Actions run step has no shell: line and runs pytest | tee log. pytest fails. What does the step report?

choices.text: Failure, since -e stops at the first failed command
choices.why: -e sees the pipeline's status, which is tee's.

choices.text: Success: bash -e {0} has no pipefail
choices.why: Right. Name the shell or start with set -euo pipefail.

choices.text: Skipped, since tee produced no artifact
choices.why: Skipping is decided by if, not by output.

choices.text: An error before the step starts
choices.why: The step runs normally.

prompt: A shell option that makes a pipeline fail if any command in it failed is ___ .
In run 4, which cells failed?

choices.text: Only Python 3.11
choices.why: All three Pythons failed in UTC.

choices.text: Every UTC cell
choices.why: Right. The failure followed the zone and ignored the version.

choices.text: Every São Paulo cell
choices.why: Those passed, like the laptop.

choices.text: All six
choices.why: Three passed.

prompt: Why did the dispatch tests pass on Ana's laptop after the zone was removed?

choices.text: Because the tests were skipped locally
choices.why: 3 passed, none skipped.

choices.text: Because the laptop has Python 3.13
choices.why: Every Python failed in UTC.

choices.text: The laptop's clock is set to São Paulo
choices.why: Right. Without a zone, fromtimestamp reads the machine's.

choices.text: Because the CI clock is wrong
choices.why: UTC is a correct setting, and a common one for servers.

prompt: Three Python versions, two time zones and two database versions. How many cells?
A project supports Python 3.9 to 3.13. Which versions does the lesson suggest putting in the matrix?

choices.text: Only 3.13, the newest
choices.why: The oldest is where a too-new feature breaks.

choices.text: All five
choices.why: Possible, but the lesson suggests the edges to keep cells few.

choices.text: The oldest and newest
choices.why: Right. Test the edges of each axis.

choices.text: Whichever the developers use
choices.why: That is the configuration the laptop already tests.

prompt: Why does the hook keep a JUnit XML file per cell?

choices.text: Because pytest refuses to run without one
choices.why: It is optional.

choices.text: Services read it to list failures
choices.why: Right. It turns a log into a table on a web page.

choices.text: To make the run faster next time
choices.why: It is a report, not a cache.

choices.text: To store the coverage data
choices.why: Coverage keeps its own files.

prompt: With fail-fast on, what would run 4 have hidden?

choices.text: That the commit was broken
choices.why: The first red cell shows that.

choices.text: The pattern by time zone
choices.why: Right. Cancelled cells hide the pattern that pointed at the zone.

choices.text: The name of the failing test
choices.why: The first failing cell names it.

choices.text: Nothing, the lab's hook never cancels
choices.why: The question is about turning it on.

prompt: Why was the dispatch change reverted rather than patched in place?

choices.text: Because git cannot patch a pushed commit
choices.why: It can add a new commit on top.

choices.text: Because the simplification was forbidden
choices.why: It can come back with the zone and a UTC test.

choices.text: It restores a known-good commit
choices.why: Right. Run 5 confirmed it.

choices.text: To delete run 4's logs
choices.why: The logs stay under ~/ci/runs/4.

prompt: Installing from the warm cache took how many seconds of real time?
A cache is keyed only on the runner's operating system. A pin in requirements-dev.txt changes. What happens?

choices.text: Stale packages are restored
choices.why: Right. The key must change when the pins change.

choices.text: The cache is rebuilt automatically
choices.why: Nothing in the key changed, so nothing triggers a rebuild.

choices.text: The run fails with a cache error
choices.why: It restores silently.

choices.text: Nothing, caches only hold timing data
choices.why: It holds packages.

prompt: Which of these should not be cached between runs?

choices.text: Downloaded packages, keyed on the lock file
choices.why: That is the textbook cache.

choices.text: A tool's binary at a pinned version
choices.why: Pinned and expensive: a good candidate.

choices.text: A test database left by the last run
choices.why: Right. The run would stop starting from what was committed.

choices.text: Compiled third-party dependencies
choices.why: Derived from pins and slow to build: cacheable.

prompt: Why did the set-to-list test pass five times and fail five times?

choices.text: Because zone_of is random
choices.why: zone_of always gives SP and SE for those CEPs.

choices.text: Set order changes per process
choices.why: Right. PYTHONHASHSEED=0 froze it, which is not the fix.

choices.text: Because the CI was busy
choices.why: It ran ten times on one quiet machine.

choices.text: Because pytest shuffles tests
choices.why: There is one test in the file.

prompt: What is the right fix for that test?

choices.text: Set PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in the pipeline
choices.why: That freezes an accident; the test still asserts an order nobody promised.

choices.text: Retry it until it passes
choices.why: That turns red into try again.

choices.text: Compare sorted(seen)
choices.why: Right. Assert what the code promises, whatever the order.

choices.text: Delete it
choices.why: It checks something real once fixed.

prompt: Was the UTC failure of run 4 a flaky test?

choices.text: Yes, it failed in some cells and not others
choices.why: It failed in every UTC cell and passed in every São Paulo cell, every time.

choices.text: No: deterministic per environment
choices.why: Right. Same environment, same answer; the matrix showed the dependency.

choices.text: Yes, because time is involved
choices.why: Time made it environment-dependent, not random.

choices.text: Impossible to say from the run
choices.why: The pattern across six cells says it.

prompt: How many seconds did the timed push of run 5 take, rounded to one decimal?
If the six cells ran in parallel on six machines, roughly how long would the test part of run 5 take?

choices.text: The sum of the six, about 10 seconds
choices.why: That is the sequential cost.

choices.text: The slowest cell, about 2 seconds
choices.why: Right. A parallel run takes as long as its slowest cell.

choices.text: The fastest cell, about 1.4 seconds
choices.why: The run waits for every cell.

choices.text: The same 13.3 seconds
choices.why: Parallelism removes the waiting between cells.

prompt: What happens to a team when the checks that gate a merge take well over ten minutes, by the lesson?

choices.text: Tests get more thorough
choices.why: Duration does not add thoroughness.

choices.text: The runner bill falls
choices.why: Longer runs cost more.

choices.text: People stop waiting and batch changes
choices.why: Right. The opposite of integrating continuously.

choices.text: Flaky tests disappear
choices.why: Nothing about duration fixes flakiness.

prompt: What makes a check required on a hosted service?

choices.text: A repository setting
choices.why: Right. The merge button stays disabled.

choices.text: Naming the job required in the workflow
choices.why: Required is a property of the repository, not of a job's name.

choices.text: Running it on a schedule
choices.why: Schedules do not gate merges.

choices.text: Giving it a longer timeout
choices.why: Timeouts do not make it required.

prompt: Main just went red. Order the team's moves as the lesson describes.
items: Stop starting new work on top of it
Revert the change that broke it
Confirm the next run is green
Bring the change back with a fix and a test
trap: The fix comes back last; first main has to be green again.

prompt: A branch lives three weeks and its first run on main goes red. Why is it hard to find the cause?

choices.text: Because the CI deletes old logs
choices.why: The logs are there; the problem is the size of the change.

choices.text: Too many changes integrate at once
choices.why: Right. Small changes merged daily make a result point at a cause.

choices.text: Because branches cannot be tested
choices.why: The hook ignores them; hosted CI tests pull requests.

choices.text: Because three weeks exceeds the cache lifetime
choices.why: Caching does not decide whether a cause can be found.

prompt: Match each run of the lab's CI to what it showed.

pairs.right: A file that was never committed

prompt: A team's pipeline is green but a release fails because a test reads a date with the machine's zone. The pipeline runs only in America/Sao_Paulo. What change does this lesson suggest?

choices.text: Set every server to São Paulo time
choices.why: That hides the dependency until the next server.

choices.text: Add a UTC axis and name the zone
choices.why: Right. The axis catches it next time; the fix removes the dependency.

choices.text: Retry the release
choices.why: The failure is deterministic.

choices.text: Mark the test flaky and quarantine it
choices.why: It is not flaky.
